title: Volatility as a Signal Switch: Regime-dependent Intraday Mean Reversion in Nasdaq-100 Futures
abstract: We ask whether intraday price moves beyond an implied-volatility&nbsp; <br> band in E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures (NQ) revert before the session&nbsp; <br> closes. The band is set daily as ± VXN/16 relative to the&nbsp; <br> prior-session close; dividing by 16 converts the annualised VXN&nbsp; <br> to a one-day standard-deviation estimate. Over 860 algorithmically&nbsp; <br> detected band-breach events (2018–2026), the unconditional&nbsp; <br> same-session reversion rate is 85.2%. When we sort by VXN level,&nbsp; <br> the Sharpe–VXN profile is non-monotone. Reversion probability is&nbsp; <br> statistically significant in all four VXN buckets (BH-adjusted&nbsp; <br> p &lt; 0.001), but the 30-minute exit rule generates positive Sharpe&nbsp; <br> only at the extremes (VXN &lt; 20: 0.38; VXN &gt;= 30: 0.64), with&nbsp; <br> slightly negative values in between. Walk-forward validation&nbsp; <br> confirms the pattern out of sample (IS 2018–2022, n = 298,&nbsp; <br> Sharpe = 0.47; OOS 2023–2026, n = 191, Sharpe = 1.29). A&nbsp; <br> pre-sample from 2010–2017 gives a Sharpe of -0.94 without the&nbsp; <br> regime filter. A momentum alternative that enters in the breach&nbsp; <br> direction is rejected on the same data. The band effect depends&nbsp; <br> on volatility, with the strongest edge appearing when VXN &gt;= 30.
